It's tradition vs. progress; on which side will you stand? |game = The Sims 3 Store |housed residents = 49 |cost = N/A |homepage = https://store.thesims3.com/dragonvalley.html }}{{Official item|TS3|store}}[[File:Dragon Valley Reflect.png|left]]'''Dragon Valley''' is a ''The Sims 3 ''Store [[world]] that was released on May 30, 2013.[https://beyondsims.com/47295/dragon-valley-release-date-revealed/ Article about Maxis confirmation of release] on [[BeyondSims]] It was first announced at the Live Broadcast on April 16, 2013. The theme of this [[world]] is medieval and fantasy. It features brand new locations, features, as well as new characters. == Description == [[File:Dragon Valley Logo.png|left|75px]] ''Welcome to Dragon Valley, a land of myth and fantasy. It's been years since any adult dragons have terrorized this peaceful town but it's not yet time to rest. The [[Elf|elven]] Sims of Dragon Valley are working to ensure that their military is up to par, their citizens are prepared for disaster, and that the scientific techniques they've used to keep the dragonlings small stay intact. The skies may be clear for now, but beneath the surface a conflict is brewing between the Mithrillen and O'Connell families for control of the town. It's tradition vs. progress: on which side will you stand?'' {{clr}} == Backstory == [[File:Backstory Render DV.png|right]] ;Open Your Eyes! You all walk around with [[dragon]]s on your arms as pets. But don't you see? We're just recovering; we've finally rebuilt after the original Dragons ravaged our land. The O'Connells "land" in our world with their way of taming dragons and we've been following them ever since! When it was we Mithrilens that used to keep the town safe! Don't let them pull the wool over your eyes. Just look at the dragons. They are supposed to be "babies" but each one does something more dastardly than the last! This will only end in misery. Let me help you. The Mithrilen family knows our ways, our traditions, and our bond with the land. Let me guide you to safety, before it's too late. ;Mithrilen for Mayor ;Before it's too late. {{clr}} == Lots == 82 lots in total are in Dragon Valley: 27 commercial, 22 empty and 33 residential lots. The page had a glitch that allowed some people to purchase and download an incomplete version of the world. The glitch was soon fixed, but Maxis staff strongly recommended that players uninstall the incomplete version.[https://simsvip.com/2013/05/10/simgurutatertot-speaks-on-dragon-valley-early-release/ SimGuruTaterTot Speaks on Dragon Valley Early Release] on [https://simsvip.com/ SimsVIP.com] *There is an additional venue available from the Store, [https://store.thesims3.com/setsProductDetails.html?productId=OFB-SIM3:65646 The Duke of Bows Renaissance Faire], which was designed specifically for use in Dragon Valley. However, it must be purchased separately and is not included in the Gold Edition. Instead, buying the Gold Edition from the Store grants the purchaser enough additional SimPoints to buy the venue, and the write-up for the package explicitly recommends this. *The Gold Edition version sold in the Store includes an extra set called [https://store.thesims3.com/setsProductDetails.html?productId=OFB-SIM3:65137 Celtic Lands]. The physical retail edition of the World includes an additional download code in the box, which must be redeemed separately in order to access the Celtic Lands extra features. The box edition does not, however, include additional SimPoints, as the Store edition does, making the box edition somewhere between the Standard and Gold editions from the Store. ==Namings== *The names Dagda, Lugh, Brighid, are taken from Celtic Mythology. *Morrigan O'Reilly shares her name with one of the most important Goddesses of Celtic Mythology. *There's a street named Shillelagh Street, which is one of the drinks served by a [[Mixology (The Sims 3)|mixologist]]. *The Hooley and Dolan families are a parody of the tales [[wikipedia:Robin Hood|Robin Hood]] and [[wikipedia:Little Red Riding Hood|Little Red Riding Hood]], respectively. *The Sackholme family is a parody of Sookie and Jason Stackhouse from the ''True Blood'' TV series. *The O'Connell family is either a parody of Mérida and her family from Disney/Pixar's ''Brave'', or a parody of ''Dragonriders of Pern'''s Connell family. *The MacAnna sisters could be a reference to either Lewis Carroll's, or Tim Burton's movie adaptation of, the White Queen & Red Queen, which are often portrayed respectively as good (Shannon) and bad (Teagan). *Aislin Walsh is probably a spoof of Mrs. Lovett, from Sweeney Todd. She may also be a female spoof of Sweeney Todd himself, given her description. ==Trivia== *The [[theatre]] in Dragon Valley is based on the World Theatre and its counterpart in SimCity, both of which are based on Shakespeare's Globe Theatre in London, England. *It is unknown if the [[Elf|elves]] of Dragon Valley are related in any way to the Blue Elves found in a Sims Medieval chance card that may appear upon "Tak[ing] a Stroll" in the forest, but their appearance seems to suggest so. Additionally, it is unknown if Dragon Valley is in any way related to the kingdoms of The Sims Medieval, although the "By my troth!" exclamation in the Sims 4 notification (see below) implies some connection. *In ''The Sims 4'', sometimes a sim gets a description of: "By my troth! My newest penpal resides in Dragon Valley!" when checking for penpal replies. *Dragon Valley is mentioned in [[:File:Door to Nowhere.png|Door to Nowhere]] object from ''The Sims 4: Realm of Magic''. *It is unusual as to why Jennifer and Johnny Burb resides in this world as an adult and not [[Jeff Pleasant]], [[Diane Pleasant]], [[Brad Burb]] or [[Tiffany Burb]] as a child as ''[[The Sims 3]]'' takes place before the events of ''[[The Sims]]'', meaning Jennifer would not be born yet. However, [[Barnacle Bay]] does take place after the events of ''[[The Sims 2]]'' so it's possible that Sunlit Tides takes place between the events of ''The Sims'' and ''The Sims 2'' as [[Lucy Burb]] is not born yet and Jennifer and Johnny are not married yet, however there is no confirmation of this. **An adult [[Daniel Pleasant]] and [[Mary-Sue Pleasant]] also appear in [[Sunlit Tides]] without Diane or Jeff, which could also put Dragon Valley in the same possible timeline as Sunlit Tides as it should be noted [[Angela Pleasant]] and [[Lilith Pleasant]] are not born yet. *While some houses do have a TV, consumer [[SimNation#Technology|technology]] is less common than most other worlds. *Parking space is entirely absent in the neighborhood, despite at least one Sim in the neighborhood (Emma Delaney) having the Vehicle Enthusiast trait. == Gallery == Images = The Sims 3 Dragon Valley Cover.jpg|Store Version Cover HomepageSplash_DragonValleyPreLaunch.png DragonValleyCoastline.jpg|The panoramic view of Dragon Valley Dragon Valley buildings TS3.jpg DragonValleyHouse.jpg Red dragon in flight.jpg Dragon themed bedroom TS3.jpg Dragon Valley boulders.jpg Female Sim in Dragon Valley TS3.jpg BurnedByDragon.jpg DragonValleyCottage.jpg Dragon Valley buildings.jpg DragonValleyRocks.jpg the-sims-3-dragon-valley.png Dragon Valley EA Store cover.jpg|The cover image on EA Store. |-| Videos = The Sims 3 Dragon Valley Trailer|Dragon Valley Trailer ==Other languages== Since it is rare for ''The Sims 3'' world names to be translated, only the differing names are listed below. {| class="wikitable sortable" ! Midnight Hollow.text:
{{Pagecover |image = World_ScreenshotWeb_MidnightHollow001.jpg |pagetype = Downloadable [[World]] |subtitle = |TS3SE|gen = TS3|offset = 55}} {{Infobox world |name = Midnight Hollow |image = [[File:Midnight Hollow thumbnail.png|250px]] |caption = Explore a landscape where all you're really required to be is yourself. Under the subdued sky of Midnight Hollow, it's the residents who really shine. Eccentric townsfolk have taken a century-old Victorian town and made it a place they can call home. What life will you make in a town where creativity and individuality are at the center of it all? |game = The Sims 3 Store |housed residents = 51 |cost = 2426 (3524 for Gold) |homepage = https://store.thesims3.com/midnighthollow.html?productId=OFB-SIM3:68670 |skies = Extremely dark clouds }} {{Distinguish|Forgotten Hollow}} {{Official item|TS3|store}}[[File:Midnight Hollow Reflect.png|left]]'''Midnight Hollow''' is a [[world]] from ''[[The Sims 3 Store]]'' that was released on September 26, 2013. It was first announced on September 12, 2013. This world is based on various sleepy towns from classical monochrome horror movies. The whole town has a dull and darkened color scheme. It features brand new locations, new retail businesses, and new characters. ==Description== [[File:Midnight Hollow Logo.png|75px|left]] ''Find your light in the dark splendor of Midnight Hollow'' ''Explore a landscape where all you're really required to be is yourself. Under the subdued sky of Midnight Hollow, it's the residents who really shine. Eccentric townsfolk have taken a century-old Victorian town and made it a place they can call home. What life will you make in a town where creativity and individuality are at the center of it all?'' ''Will you be the owner of an art gallery bringing culture to the town? Or run a vintage furniture boutique to add class to Sims homes? Or a car showroom showing Sims life in the fast lane? The business opportunities are endless!'' {{clr}} ==Backstory== [[File:Backstory Render MH.png|right]] '''It's Rarely Sunny in Midnight Hollow!''' Hello there friend, * Are you sick of feeling out of place? * Sick of feeling bad that there's no one around like you? * Sick of those smiling neighbors telling you to enjoy the "[[Sunset Valley|sunset" in the "valley?"]] Then come to '''Midnight Hollow''' where it's good to be one of a kind! Life is hard and people will always have something to say about you. "All of her husbands die mysteriously and suddenly" or "I think her [[Nervous Subject|son]] was fathered by the [[Grim Reaper]]" or "[[Olive Specter/theories|I'm pretty sure she's a murderer]]" ...Where do they come up with this stuff?? I moved here to get away from the "normal" life to find a life that's normal for me. Let them have their [[Starlight Shores|"Starlight" and "shores,"]] I'll take my century-old Victorian mansion, eerie landscape and interesting neighbors every time. Here's hoping you're next! - I meant being my new neighbor; not the whole murder thing FYI. See you at Midnight Hollow! ''-- [[Olive Specter]]'' {{clrr}} ==Cultural references== Like many worlds in ''The Sims 3'', Midnight Hollow contains various references to real world culture. For example, the [[Yates family]] are a spoof of Norman and Norma Bates from the ''[[wikipedia:Psycho (franchise)|Psycho]]'' franchise, [[Lucien Hyde]] might be a spoof of shock rocker Marilyn Manson, and [[Julian Poirot]] shares his last name with Hercule Poirot from [[wikipedia:Agatha Christie|Agatha Christie]]'s mystery novels. He might also be a reference to [[wikipedia:Pierrot|Pierrot]], the classic sad clown from [[wikipedia:Commedia dell'arte|Commedia dell'arte]]. The names [[John Doe]] and [[Jane Doe]] are used as placeholder for a party whose true identity is unknown or must be withheld in a legal action, case, or discussion in many English-speaking nations. The names are also used to refer to a corpse or hospital patient whose identity is unknown. The [[Flynn family (The Sims 3)|Flynn family]] may be a spoof of the Baudelaire family from the book series ''[[wikipedia:A Series of Unfortunate Events|A Series of Unfortunate Events]]'', written by [[wikipedia:Lemony Snicket|Lemony Snicket]]. Also, many of the community locations are named in the same alliterative style that is used by Lemony Snicket in the same series, and there is also a large burnt house at the end of a street which may be a reference to the Baudelaire mansion. Also, in the forest with red grass next to the house Winchester, there is a standing lamp, which is clearly a reference to the Chronicles of Narnia. Mr. Hyde is a reference to Jekyll and Hyde. The Winchester house may be a reference to the Winchester brothers in the TV show Supernatural, or to the house of Sarah Winchester, wife of treasurer of the Winchester Repeating Arms Company, William Winchester. She famously built the Winchester Mystery House, supposedly being instructed to by spirits. The [[Lau family]] appear to be a parody of ''[[wikipedia:The Powerpuff Girls|The Powerpuff Girls]]''. The [[business]] [[Rabbit Hole|office]], Simagon Alley, is also a spoof, in this case of [[w:c:Harrypotter:Diagon Alley|Diagon Alley]] from the ''[[wikipedia:Harry Potter|Harry Potter]]'' series. ==Lots== {{Main|List of uninhabited Midnight Hollow lots}} Midnight Hollow has a total of 92 lots consisting of 55 residential lots (25 occupied, 13 unoccupied and 17 empty) and 37 community lots (32 with items and 5 empty). {{clrr}} ===Residential=== {|class="wikitable sortable small-text-cells" style="width:100%" |+Residential Lots |- ! scope="col"|Address ! scope="col"|Lot Name ! scope="col"| Resident Household ! scope="col"|BR ! scope="col"|BA ! scope="col"|Cost ! scope="col"|Unfurn.

She doesn't like neighbors or visitors or the outdoors or children. All she likes is reading books and being alone. To be honest, no one in town really knows what Eliza looks like let alone how she's fairing and that's the way she likes it. '' * '''[[Phineas Bledsoe|Bledsoe family]]''' ''125 Poffald Place'' :§12,000 :Difficulty: 1 :[[Phineas Bledsoe]] :''Phineas is at the height of fashion and the height of poetry (if there ever was one). He can tell in an instant if a piece of writing or clothing will be a hit or a gauche rerun to be quickly forgotten by the masses. It's best to get and stay on his good side if you want near the "it" list.'' * '''[[Kara Carter|Carter family]]''' ''80 True Terrace'' :§3,000 :Difficulty: 1 :[[Kara Carter]] :''Kara Carter is a leading chef in town with an eccentric sense of fashion. She grabs inspiration where she can find it, whether it's the modern Vivienne Simwood, or Marie Simtoinette of the past. She may be described as "Shabby Chic" but her Goopy Carbonara is to DIE FOR.'' * '''[[Doe family]]''' ''25 Swallow Street'' :§30,000 :Difficulty: 5 :[[John Doe]], [[Jane Doe]], [[Joseph Doe]], [[Jennifer Doe]], [[James Doe]] :''Jane is the perfect housewife, from her neat hairstyle to her fashionable yet conservative dress. She's neat, nurturing, loves her kids, and can make a mean pot roast! Meanwhile, John is rising in the ranks at his corporate job. He feels successful in life and supported by his family. He works hard but comes home in enough time to teach his kids a lesson or two about life and talk to his wife about her day. Nothing mysterious seems to be happening here, but didn't their house used to have a basement? '' * '''[[Entrepreneurs household]]''' ''30 Swallow Street'' :§5,000 :Difficulty: 2 :[[Todd Landgraab]], [[Karl Simon]], [[Seema Sielen]] :''Seema has the charm, Karl has the smarts, and Todd has the money. They're pressured by friends, family, and society to make something of themselves and they have a plan! Entrepreneurship is a real thing...right?'' * '''[[Conrad Finley|Finley family]]''' ''87 True Terrace'' :§3,000 :Difficulty: 1 :[[Conrad Finley]] :''Conrad was born for the evening news. He has the wit, the brains, and the nose for news. The only things he's lacking in the world is melanin. But he doesn't miss it and he's not letting it hold him back. He'll be the anchor on the evening news in the next 5 years or his name isn't Conrad Finley.'' * '''[[Flynn family (The Sims 3)|Flynn family]]''' ''121 Poffald Place'' :§2,000 :Difficulty: 4 :[[Edmund Flynn]], [[Maggie Flynn]], [[Mitchell Flynn]], [[Cora Flynn]] :''When Jackson Bishop received a letter from the Flynn estate lawyer detailing the poor, rich orphans who were coming to live with their long lost Uncle they've never met, he decided this was his chance to improve his standing and become guardians of the children for their fortune. Good old Edmund Flynn passed in a tragic accident and the kids *did* need a guardian after all. He's just being charitable!...right.'' * '''[[Lucien Hyde|Hyde family]]''' ''75 Breach Bend'' :§10,000 :Difficulty: 1 :[[Lucien Hyde]] :''Lucien is a tortured artist whose only torturer is himself. '' * '''[[Lau family]]''' ''123 Poffald Place'' :§8,000 :Difficulty: 2 :[[Mai Lau]], [[Annie Lau]], [[Lucy Lau]] :''The Lau triplets were the foremost scientists in the field of optimizing the human body to better the earth. After an experiment went awry the women were left with super fit physiques and the need for a new purpose in life. Each sister took on a new career that would employ their newfound physical prowess.'' * '''[[Jack Limb|Limb family]]''' ''45 Breach Bend'' :§3,000 :Difficulty: 1 :[[Jack Limb]] :''Jack is the resident toy collector. New in Box, Vintage, First Edition, are all phrases in his vocabulary and he keeps his collection pristine. He'd like to go into toy making but lacks the proper skill, so in the meantime he's drafting a daring rescue of his dear love Sarah from the evil Dr. Synapse.'' * '''[[Samantha Nguyen|Nguyen family]]''' ''26 Swallow Street'' :§3,000 :Difficulty: 1 :[[Samantha Nguyen]] :''Samantha has a number of tattoos on her body and each one tells a story of something she's loved, places she's been, and where she hopes to be. Midnight Hollow is just one stop on her grand adventure of bringing affordable medicine to the world and who knows where she's headed next.'' * '''[[Trang Pham|Pham family]]''' ''103 Shearin Stroll'' :§7,000 :Difficulty: 1 :[[Trang Pham]] :''Trang is an artistic savant. She paints some of the most brilliant paintings in the world and is renowned for her unqiue avant garde style. It's really too bad that she can't stand art. At all. '' * '''[[Julian Poirot|Poirot family]]''' ''77 Breach Bend'' :§3,000 :Difficulty: 1 :[[Julian Poirot]] :''Julian has been a performer all of his life. He shined on the stages of Champs Les Sims and brought wonder and excitement to all those who viewed him. But those watching him didn't know that the light they saw on stage was not talent, but the light actually inside his heart. As time wore on and life got harder his light began to fade and performances became more and more sad. Can love bring Julian's light back? An impoverished childhood didn't prepare him for the success that would find him in his later life. Now that he has a small fortune he intends to keep it. No point in wasting money on fancy furnishing or an expensive car. He will only buy the cheapest that money can buy, because he never wants to be poor again.'' * '''[[Winchester family]]''' ''124 Poffald Place'' :§6,000 :Difficulty: 2 :[[Cedrick Winchester]], [[Odessa Winchester]] :''Odessa and Cedrick come from a long line of blue-blooded royals but had their throne usurped when the townsfolk felt that they were a bit too crazy to be rulers. They've found a town where they feel comfortable and they're trying their hand at Politics. Royalty here, Royalty there, what does it matter when you're royalty?'' * '''[[Yates family]]''' ''11 Swallow Street'' :§3,000 :Difficulty: 2 :[[Viola Yates]], [[Morgan Yates]] :''Morgan loves his mother. [[File:Roaring Heights Reflect.png|left]] '''Roaring Heights''' is the eleventh and final [[world]] available from ''[[The Sims 3 Store]]''<ref>[https://twitter.com/SimGuruCopeland/status/476059667043328000 SimGuruCopeland's tweet] on [https://www.twitter.com Twitter]</ref>. It was released for ''[[The Sims 3]]'' on December 12, 2013, after being announced on November 25, 2013. Roaring Heights is a seaside city that consists of an urban center with high-rise buildings, surrounded by suburban neighborhoods and coastal areas. The world introduces several premium objects and exclusive gameplay features. The world features an Art Deco theme influenced by American culture from the 1920s to the 1940s, reflected in its architecture, objects, clothing, and Sims.

==Description==
[[File:Roaring Heights Logo.png|left|75px]]
'''Elevate your lifestyle to new heights'''

''Welcome to a city where bold shapes, rich colors, and lavish looks rule the skyline! The residents of Roaring Heights are living in the fast lane in this booming place filled with striking skyscrapers and bustling beaches. Whether you’re content to hang out on the piers, work your way to the top, or host glamorous parties at home, there’s a place for every lifestyle. With endless opportunities at your front door, which new life will you choose in Roaring Heights?''
{{clr}}

==Price==
Like [[Monte Vista]] and [[Dragon Valley]], Roaring Heights is purchased using real-world currency rather than [[SimPoint]]s. It is sold in two bundles: the Standard Bundle, which includes Roaring Heights and 100 SimPoints, and the Gold Bundle, which includes Roaring Heights, 1,900 SimPoints, and the Boardwalk Attire clothing set.

The current price for the Standard Bundle is US$19.99, while the Gold Bundle costs US$34.99.

==Backstory==
[[File:Backstory Render RH.png|right]]

'''Greetings from Roaring Heights!'''

We’ve been on vacation in Roaring Heights for a few days and can’t believe we didn’t come here sooner! The pier quickly became our favorite place to eat, with its romantic sunsets and proximity to the beach. Once the sun is down, the downtown bustles with activity!

Ever since its humble beginnings, the residents of Roaring Heights have embraced the art deco style, which still remains very influential to this city. We adore the pastel and neon lit buildings dotting the beachfront and distinctive style of the extravagant skyscrapers.

We’re loving this place so much that we’ve already begun to look at available real estate. The houses are so unique; we’ve never seen anything like them! It’ll be a blast living here, and we hope you will soon be our neighbor!

''-- [[Contessa Capp|Contessa]] & [[Consort Capp]]''
{{clr}}

==Cultural references==
Roaring Heights is themed after American culture, fashion, and architecture from the 1920s through the 1940s, particularly the Art Deco movement. The world's name is likely a reference to the "[[wikipedia:Roaring Twenties|Roaring Twenties]]", a term used to describe Western culture and society during the 1920s. Many of Roaring Heights' pre-made Sims are references to celebrities, characters, and cultural figures from the era.

Reflecting its early 20th century inspiration, most buildings in Roaring Heights lack modern technology, such as [[TV|television]]s, [[computer]]s, and [[stereo]]s, making it one of the most historically distinct worlds in The Sims 3. A notable exception is the Downtown Museum, which contains functional televisions and stereos.

According to SimGuruTaterTot and SimGuruBrett during [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QvQEL6IiL1Y "The Sims 3 Live Broadcast - Roaring Heights Gameplay" video], the world's layout and architecture were inspired by Miami, New York City, and Chicago. The city hall is based on Buffalo City Hall, while the lighthouse is based on a lighthouse in Kálfshamarsvík, Iceland. [[Beach Drive]] also resembles Ocean Drive in Miami.

==Families==
===New Families===
*'''[[Ainsley Andrews|Andrews family]]''' ''33 Palm Tree Avenue''
:§2,000
:Difficulty: 1
:[[Ainsley Andrews]]
:''Ainsley is a photographic genius with her ability to take pictures of the environment that make you think you’re truly there! Others around town love her positive attitude. Can Ainsley maintain a balance of increasing popularity and her photography or will something have to give?''

*'''[[Astare household]]''' ''38 Van Alen Street''
:§25,000
:Difficulty: 2
:[[Frank Astare]], [[Judy Rogers]]
:''Already a star in her own right, Judy never shined brighter than when she and Frank danced together. Frank may lack curb appeal, but is flowing with talent. Can these two stars shine even brighter or are they doomed to fizzle out?''

*'''[[Francisco Battista|Battista family]]''' ''45 Beach Drive''
:§4,500
:Difficulty: 1
:[[Francisco Battista]]
:''Francisco is the painter of his time and he knows it. Like every great genius, he’s also got a screw or two loose as evidenced by him being in the local newspaper due to some unusual behavior. Will Francisco straighten up or is this just the beginning?''

*'''[[Samantha Cassat|Cassat family]]''' ''52 Sunburst Street''
:§2,200
:Difficulty: 1
:[[Samantha Cassat]]
:''With her beautiful looks and brilliant mind, Samantha can get any man she wants. Her latest affair in the office with David Morgan left her pregnant and David’s wife without a clue. Were Samantha and David meant for each other or was this just another torrid affair?''

*'''[[Michael Dandy|Dandy family]]''' ''24 Riverside Terrace''
:§47,500
:Difficulty: 1
:[[Michael Dandy]]
:''Michael never had an easy life and every Simoleon he has required hard work with an occasional crime on the side. Though he feels guilty, Michael does this all for the secret love of his life. Will Michael finally be able to make his love public?''

*'''[[Davidson household]]''' ''47 Sunburst Street''
:§5,000
:Difficulty: 2
:[[Norma Davidson]], [[Gil McGinnis]]
:''Gil and Norma are two Sims who met under strange circumstances. Norma obsessively awaits for the days of her big silver screen comeback and Gill, while down on his luck, was taken in by Norma. Can Gil repair Norma’s fragile state of mind and help Norma make a comeback?''

*'''[[Davis household (Roaring Heights)|Davis household]]''' ''27 Palm Tree Avenue''
:§20,000
:Difficulty: 2
:[[Bonnie Davis (Roaring Heights)|Bonnie Davis]], [[Clyde Reeves]]
:''When Bonnie and Clyde met, it was love at first sight. Clyde is a natural daredevil who’s shown Bonnie a new side of life. Bonnie is an aspiring writer and loves to write about their exploits. Will Clyde eventually lead Bonnie down the wrong path?''

*'''[[Davis-Welles family]]''' ''40 Palm Tree Avenue''
:§27,000
:Difficulty: 2
:[[Mark Davis-Welles]], [[Rita Davis-Welles]]
:''On the outside, Rita and Mark appear to be a happily married couple but they’ve both fallen in love with other people. Will they risk scandal or work to stay together?''

*'''[[Harbucks household]]''' ''36 Loewy Lane''
:§200,000
:Difficulty: 2
:[[Olivier Harbucks]], [[Shirley Templeton]]
:''Although Olivier had more money and possessions than ever, he was missing one thing – a family. Fate took a strange turn when one day an orphan named Shirley appeared on his doorstep. Will Olivier finally help Shirley realize her dreams of stardom?''

*'''[[Houveir family]]''' ''32 Riverside Terrace''
:§40,000
:Difficulty: 2
:[[Clark Houveir]], [[Louise Houveir]]
:''Clark is a man who gets what he wants, including Louise who puts on a fake smile, much to her dismay. Clark is too busy cooking up the next scheme and Louise desperately wants attention. Can this odd couple stay together or was their marriage doomed to fail from the start?''

*'''[[Jones family (Roaring Heights)|Jones family]]''' ''22 Palm Tree Avenue''
:§15,000
:Difficulty: 3
:[[Beverly Jones]], [[Helen Jones]], [[Edward Jones (Roaring Heights)|Edward Jones]]
:''Beverly is a fashion queen who has everything “en mode” except her children, thanks to the sudden death of her husband. Her son Edward turns a blind eye towards fashion and her daughter Helen wants nothing more than some attention from Beverly. Will Beverly find a new husband to save her family?''

*'''[[LaFontaine family]]''' ''24 Palm Tree Avenue''
:§1,700
:Difficulty: 2
:[[Thomas LaFontaine]], [[Elizabeth LaFontaine]]
:''Elizabeth wants a simple life, without distractions like affection for others, yet her father Thomas firmly disagrees. Worried that she’ll be Simoleonless and alone, Thomas is committed to finding her a husband. Will true love ever find Elizabeth or will a forced marriage create a rift between Elizabeth and Thomas?''

*'''[[Marks family]]''' ''39 Palm Tree Avenue''
:§4,000
:Difficulty: 4
:[[Sharpo Marks]], [[Glummo Marks]], [[Dyno Marks]], [[Sneako Marks]], [[Grumpo Marks]]
:''This set of brothers are distinct in their own way and when brought together their comedy troupe is a barrel full of laughs! Never knowing when the act is supposed to end, these brothers can’t be taken seriously. Will the Marks brothers ever grow up and act their age?''

*'''[[Meyers family]]''' ''25 Palm Tree Avenue''
:§1,200
:Difficulty: 2
:[[Ralph Meyers]], [[Irene Meyers]]
:''Love has a way of making one blind, and for Ralph this is no exception. His wife Irene is as unfaithful as they get after having many affairs due to an unhappy marriage and resentment for Ralph. Will Ralph ever open his eyes and see his wife for who she really is?''

*'''[[Morgan family]]''' ''51 Sunburst Street''
:§55,000
:Difficulty: 5
:[[David Morgan]], [[Donna Morgan]], [[Joseph Morgan]], [[Carolyn Morgan]], [[Evelyn Morgan]]
:''It would appear that David and Donna’s marriage is perfect, but in reality it’s filled with many cracks. Donna can’t bring herself to admit to seeing David and Samantha Cassat’s flirty exchanges so instead she occupies herself with her loving children. Can Donna and David keep their family together?''

*'''[[Elliot Nest|Nest family]]''' ''37 Ruhlmann Road''
:§3,000
:Difficulty: 1
:[[Elliot Nest]]
:''Throughout his life, Elliot has always been on the side of good, whether it’s stopping traffic to help an old lady cross the street or finding the owner of a stray Simoleon. He can’t stand crime of any nature and is suspicious of that Dandy guy. Will Elliot uncover the truth to Michael Dandy's wealth?''

*'''[[Picard family]]''' ''30 Riverside Terrace''
:§20,000
:Difficulty: 3
:[[Nancy Picard]], [[Gerald Picard]], [[Frances Picard]]
:''When Nancy’s husband passed away, she immediately fretted for her future and the only hope for survival lie in her children. Gerald continually rejects his mom’s attempts to send him on dates and Frances thinks her smarts will get her ahead instead of getting married. Will Nancy find another way to survive?''

*'''[[Gabe Ruth|Ruth family]]''' ''54 Sunburst Street''
:§15,000
:Difficulty: 1
:[[Gabe Ruth]]
:''The great Simbino, as he’s been known, is a national treasure. Gabe Ruth’s performance on the field is the best – bar none! Recently traded to the local Roaring Heights sports team, Gabe has much to do in a short amount of time. Will Gabe help turn around Roaring Height’s lagging team?''

*'''[[Shear family]]''' ''55 Sunburst Street''
:§5,000
:Difficulty: 3
:[[Dylan Shear]], [[Audrey Shear]], [[Charlie Shear]]
:''Dylan’s preference for wearing suits might be the scandal of the century, but she doesn’t mind. Audrey desperately wants a child, and now science has made it possible. What impact will a child have on their lives?''

*'''[[Henry Simovitch|Simovitch family]]''' ''29 Palm Tree Avenue''
:§250,000
:Difficulty: 1
:[[Henry Simovitch]]
:''Henry Simovitch is a well-known entrepreneur with a long history for technical advancement in the automobile industry. His revolutions have made him rich beyond his wildest dreams, yet he still is compelled to work the daily grind. Will Henry ever take that vacation he promised himself?''

*'''[[Theophraseus Souze|Souze family]]''' ''47 Beach Drive''
:§2,500
:Difficulty: 1
:[[Theophraseus Souze]]
:''Some say he’s a wacky doctor. Others say he’s just wacky. Whatever the case may be, Theophraseus will never give up his wacky ways. His love of medicine and making others healthy is immeasurable. Will Theophraseus’ love fizzle out trying to cure the next big disease?''

*'''[[Donia Spinelli|Spinelli family]]''' ''37 Hood Street''
:§40,000
:Difficulty: 1
:[[Donia Spinelli]]
:''Donia is bad to the bone, make no mistake about it. She doesn’t consider herself evil though. She’s simply seeing a problem and finding a way to fix it, whether it involves politicians, police officers, or nosy witnesses. Can Donia prove that she is the true leader of the town instead of Clark Houveir?''

*'''[[Virginia Supine|Supine family]]''' ''43 Beach Drive''
:§6,000
:Difficulty: 1
:[[Virginia Supine]]
:''Virginia is a famed author who settled down in Roaring Heights to continue writing, which often moves Sims with her poetic style. Brilliant and talented, her work expresses the inner most thoughts and turmoil of a woman with a secret.''

*'''[[Torrance household]]''' ''30 Palm Tree Avenue''
:§10,000
:Difficulty: 2
:[[Janet Torrance]], [[Marilyn Downes]]
:''Marilyn is a socialite who snubs the lower class, yet doesn’t know her roommate Janet comes from a lower class family despite being lifelong friends. A subtly rescued dress here and a well-made “catered” meal there kept the ruse going. Will Marilyn ever discover the hoax or can Janet keep it going forever?''

*'''[[West household]]''' ''40 Van Alen Street''
:§30,000
:Difficulty: 2
:[[May West]], [[MD Fields]]
:''These two actors are rising stars on the vaudeville scene with their mesmerizing and entertaining performances. They’ve not only won the hearts of many Sims, but also their Simoleons too! Will Mary and MD’s show continue to grow or will it become yesterday’s news?''

===Returning Families===
*'''[[Capp family]]''' ''35 Riverside Terrace''
:§60,000
:Difficulty: 4
:[[Consort Capp]], [[Contessa Capp]], [[Goneril Capp]], [[Regan Capp]]
:''After vacationing in Roaring Heights, Consort and Contessa decided to move in! With a new baby on the way, will their two children adjust to their new surroundings?''

*'''[[Thebe family]]''' ''35 Palm Tree Avenue''
:§8,000
:Difficulty: 2
:[[Hector Thebe]], [[Andromache Thebe]]
:''Hector and his wife Andromache are pleased as punch to be reunited with their son Consort in Roaring Heights. They have all sorts of plans in store for their grandchildren and not enough time! Will the Thebe’s plans go as expected or will their grandchildren pull away from them?''

==Trivia==
*The [[Capp family|Capp]] and [[Thebe family|Thebe]] families return, suggesting that the world is set before the timeline of ''[[The Sims 2]].''
*[[Roller coaster]]s return to the series for the first time since ''[[The Sims: Makin' Magic]]''. The roller coaster is included with the separately purchasable boardwalk venue.
*Sims can [[WooHoo]] in the Fixer-Upper Car, making it the first time since ''The Sims 2'' that Sims can WooHoo in cars.
*Despite being described as a city, Roaring Heights is classified internally as a suburb. As a result, [[Bridgeport]], the world introduced in ''[[The Sims 3: Late Night]]'', remains the only world internally classified as a city.
*Roaring Heights lacks a film studio rabbit hole despite several references to the film business in several Sim biographies.
*Roaring Heights is the first world in the series to feature an openly [[Same-sex relationship|same-sex couple]], [[Dylan Shear|Dylan]] and [[Audrey Shear]]. Additionally, [[Mark Davis-Welles]] and [[Rita Davis-Welles]] are married to each other while simultaneously being involved in secret same-sex affairs with [[Michael Dandy]] and [[Virginia Supine]], respectively.[[File:Roaring Heights TS4 Easter egg.jpg|thumb|220x220px|Renders of ''The Sims 4'' on Roaring Heights city hall]]
*An [[List of Easter eggs in The Sims|Easter egg]] referencing ''[[The Sims 4]]'' can be found on the Roaring Heights [[city hall]] as a mural containing Sims from ''The Sims 4''.
*The Riverside Pool might be a reference to [[Unreleased neighborhoods|Riverside]], an unreleased beta neighborhood from''[[The Sims 2]].''
*Like [[Sunlit Tides]], the biographies of Sims in Roaring Heights are determined by gender, with all male Sims sharing the same biography and all female Sims sharing another.
*Roaring Heights is the only world to include teen versions of newly added adult clothing, as well as new toddler clothes.[[File:Fiery Facade description.png|thumb]]
*Roaring Heights is referenced in the description of the "Fiery Facade" fireplace from ''[[The Sims 4: Vintage Glamour Stuff]]''. According to the description, the fireplace originally came from Roaring Heights city hall and was given as a gift to the mayor before disappearing into the architectural black market.

Champs Les Sims.text:
{{Pagecover

{{Infobox world
|name    = Champs Les Sims
|image   = [[File:Champs Les Sims thumbnail.png|250px]]
|caption = Champs Les Sims, France offers the cultural elite some of the finer things in life. Sims can learn the fine culinary art of nectar making, or flash over with a camera to learn the Photography Skill. This beautiful country town is sure to please the sense and invigorate the soul.

'''Champs Les Sims''' is a pre-made destination sub-[[world]] in ''[[The Sims 3: World Adventures]]'', alongside [[Al Simhara]] and [[Shang Simla]]. 

==Overview==
[[File:W france.png|left]] Champs Les Sims was settled towards the end of the Medieval period and has a rich history and culture. The town is modeled on rustic small towns in [[Theme (geography)#France|France]] and features activities and items that reflect French traditions. It has brick buildings and yellowish pastures. It is an excellently grape-growing country, and has a strong sense of history about it. [[Sim]]s can learn how to produce (non-alcoholic) [[nectar]] here. Sims can explore landmark [[tomb]]s and [[hidden tomb]]s throughout this world, thereby undertaking [[Opportunity/France|adventures]]. There are numerous pre-made families in Champs Les Sims, although they all lack description texts and money.

A trip to Champs Les Sims for one Sim costs [[§]]1,900 (for three days). It is the most expensive vacation destination. While visiting Champs Les Sims, Sims stay at a [[base camp]], unless they have a level three [[visa]] and have purchased a vacation home.
[[File:All France.jpg|thumb|200px]]

Commerce, community activities, and tombs are all centered on the south side of the bridge, while the [[Northbank]] only contains residential lots.

===Features===
* Sims kiss each other's cheeks to greet.
* Sims who live here all have the inheritable [[French Culture]] [[hidden trait]].
* Players' Sims can make nectar.
* Museum-style tomb adventures.

===Comparisons to Paris===
"Champs Les Sims" is French for "The Sims Fields" and is a reference to the {{WP|Champs-Élysées}}, a famous vibrant avenue in Paris. Some people might also relate Champs Les Sims to the French city of {{WP|Nîmes}}, famous for a Roman aqueduct that resembles the viaduct at the edge of town. The village also seems to be based on the French town of {{WP|Druyes-les-Belles-Fontaines}}, which also features a viaduct. Additionally, the [[bridge]] crossing the river looks almost identical to the {{WP|Pont Neuf}}, the oldest standing bridge in Paris. In Champs Les Sims, there is a viaduct with a [[Railway|train track]] running on it. Occasionally a train passes by from one tunnel to another. The train might be a reference to the Orient Express, and its model is reused from ''[[The Sims 2: FreeTime]]'' [[Desiderata Valley]] neighbourhood.

Like the other two destination worlds in ''The Sims 3: World Adventures'', Champs Les Sims has been condensed into a small town due to world size limitations:

*The [[Eiffel Tower]] can be seen from Champs Les Sims, suggesting that it is near its urban center (~15 km). However, from that same distance in Paris it is still urban.
*The river that flows through Champs Les Sims widens more like a lake outside of the world. However, the Seine river does not expand within Paris (The closest unambiguous lake on the river is in {{WP|Villiers-sur-Seine}} ~85km away).
*Chateau du Landgraab is made for ''The Sims 3'' lore.
*The Forgotten Burial Mound has elements that are not of French origin, such as a miniature [[Simhenge|Stonehenge]] at its top.
*While La Gallerie d'Art is based on the Louvre Museum in Paris, it is much smaller and it lacks a Pyramid court. Louvre Museum also does not have an underground tomb.
*The lampposts are based on some in {{WP|Saint-Germain-en-Laye}}, west of Paris.

===Exclusive Items===
* National dishes include bouillabaisse, crêpes and [[frog]] legs, new recipes for the [[Cooking (The Sims 3)|cooking]] skill.
* New [[Fishing (The Sims 3)|fishing]] and [[Collecting (The Sims 3)|collecting]] items to gather, like crawfish, frogs and snails.
* New harvestable plants: Avornalino Grapes, Cherimola Blan Grapes, Cranerlet Nuala Grapes, Gralladina Grapes, Meloire Grapes, and Renoit Grapes for [[Gardening (The Sims 3)]] skill.
* [[Book]]s that are exclusive to Champs Les Sims, including Nectar Making [[Bookstore#Skill Books|skill books]].
* Tomb survival items like the [[Shower-in-a-Can]] and [[dried food]] (Shared with the other vacation sub-worlds).
* Cheap [[camera]]s for developing the [[photography]] skill (Shared with the other vacation sub-worlds).
* [[Scooter|The Kenspa]] scooter (Shared with Al Simhara).

== The Sims 3: World Adventures (smartphone) ==
''[[The Sims 3: World Adventures (smartphone)]]'' allows the player to send their sim abroad, either for §150 for an economy [[Airport|flight]], or §250 for a first class flight. France is one of the three locations.

In France, a sim can complete two tours: Eiffel Tower<ref>https://youtu.be/jcqDB7uDjfY</ref> and Arc de Triomphe<ref>https://youtu.be/pr_cbR64NA4</ref>. Both tours are free, and consist of a presentation of various images of the site along with fun facts about it.

A sim can visit the [[Restaurant]] to purchase recipes. They can also visit the Market to buy produce, buy street food, and practice bartering, and visit the Souvenir Booth to purchase French furniture.

*Champs Les Sims is the only one of the three holiday destinations to have a castle, whereas Egypt and China have a palace.
*Champs Les Sims has the most vacation home lots of all destinations.

*The Lily Lane - Lily Court intersection appears to have a random piece of Sunset Valley-type road that goes nowhere.<ref>[https://new.reddit.com/r/thesims/comments/dme8yv/a_random_piece_of_road_in_champs_les_sims/ A random piece of road in Champs Les Sims, France.. - r/thesims]</ref> It was not reported about when World Adventures was initially released, with the earliest known notice of it being in 2015.<ref>[https://new.reddit.com/r/thesims/comments/3mmfwb/i_found_a_random_piece_of_road_in_champs_les_sims/ I found a random piece of road in Champs les Sims - r/thesims]</ref>

If you're lucky, you may even catch one of Shang Simla's famous fireworks shows! |housed residents = 33 |game = The Sims 3: World Adventures |skies = Cloudy }} '''Shang Simla''' is a pre-made destination sub-[[world]] that was added to ''[[The Sims 3]]'' in ''[[The Sims 3: World Adventures]]'' along with [[Champs Les Sims]] and [[Al Simhara]]. ==Description== [[File:W china.png|left]] Shang Simla is a peaceful community set near a mountainous area of [[wikipedia:China|China]] near the [[wikipedia:Great Wall of China|Great Wall]]. It was founded by a group of monks with an ethos of discipline and Martial Arts. The town is named after Shang Ri-La. It is full of colorful flora, such as Chinese elms and cherry trees, growing on deep green hills. This sub-hood features activities and items that compliment Chinese culture and architecture. Shang Simla is the hub for training in the [[Martial Arts]] [[skill]] introduced in ''World Adventures''. Sims can also explore landmark [[tomb]]s and [[hidden tomb]]s throughout this world, there are numerous [[Opportunity/China|adventures]] to be had. There are numerous pre-made families in Shang Simla, although they all lack description texts and money. Description text on some objects introduced in ''World Adventures'' expand on the lore of Shang Simla, depicting characters such as painter Han Shin. A trip to Shang Simla costs [[§]]1,300 for a single Sim and §1,000 for each additional Sim, making it the cheapest vacation destination the player's Sims can travel to. === Features=== *Sims will bow to each other when greeting, instead of shaking hands. *Sims who live here all have the inheritable [[Asian Culture]] [[hidden trait]]. China is one of the three locations. In China, a sim can complete two tours: Forbidden Templehttps://youtu.be/jRGtHwLqF8U and Great Wallhttps://youtu.be/oOpbI7du35k. Both tours are free, and consist of a presentation of various images of the site along with fun facts about it. A sim can visit the Language School to build their language skills. They can also visit the Market to buy produce, buy street food, or practice bartering, and can visit the Souvenir Shop to purchase Chinese furniture. ===Sims=== *Dong-Hai *Xiu-Xiu *Wong *Sun ==Comparisons with the Real World== Unlike Al Simhara and Champs Les Sims, Shang Simla has elements taken from several real world locations around [[Theme (geography)#People's Republic of China|China]], mostly from Beijing. It is set in the mountains, most likely the Taihang mountains of Hebei, Shanxi, and Shaanxi considering the Great Wall. *The Forbidden City is not a perfect square in the real world, and is located within Beijing. *The Terracotta Army in the real world is much larger than it is in game. *The Temple of Heaven in the real world does not contain an underground tomb or house a mythical axe. *In game, the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests does not exist. *The Great Wall intersects with Shang Simla. In the real world, there is no city that directly intersects The Great Wall. *There is no cave/tomb that has the head of a dragon in the real world. *Fortune cookies were not invented in People's Republic of China, and are very rare there. *The icon is a ''[[wikipedia:Torii|torii]]'' gate, which is actually [[wikipedia:Japan|Japanese]], not Chinese. Also, koi [[Fishing (The Sims 3)|fishes]] can be found in Shang Simla, which are domesticated carp found in Japan. *One of the pre-made families, the [[Kim family (Shang Simla)|Kim family]], has a Korean surname, as is the first names of at least one (possibly more) of the three members, [[Ho Sung Kim]]. Though there is a [[:wikipedia:Koreans in China|small Korean minority]] in the northeast of PRC, Kim is distinctly of Korean origin as a family name. *The "Zen" moodlet for the [[Chinese garden]] uses "Namaste!" as its main greeting, a phrase from Hindi, an India/Pakistan-based language generally not spoken in China. ==Trivia== *The [[Writing (The Sims 3)|writing]] skill [[opportunity]] "Deliver a Book to China" is about several of the Sim's books having been banned there and that the Sim must smuggle one of his/her books there, parodying real-life media bans in the People's Republic of China. *Shang Simla is mentioned in ''[[The Sims 3: Generations]]''. If a Sim makes a [[prank call]], it may be about Shang Simla as the victim of the prank call will say they don't want a free trip to Shang Simla after saying they felt hurt that the caller would think they would fall for it. *In ''[[The Sims 4: Movie Hangout Stuff]]'', there is an item called "[[:File:Lilacs & Lanterns.png|Lilacs & Lanterns]]" mentioning Shang Simla, 73 South Shang Simla Hills, and Maya Wang. According to the description, Maya Wang was part of season 4, episode 1 of ''[[Plumbob Pickers]]''. It is unknown whether she played herself, or was portrayed by someone else. *In ''[[The Sims 4: Romantic Garden Stuff]]'', there is a [[fountain]] called the "Spitting Flower Fountain" which is said to be inspired by the countryside of Shang Simla. ==Gallery== Screenshots= ChinaBridge.jpg Templeofheavenview.jpg|Shang Simla from the balcony at the top of The Temple of Heaven China Great View.jpg|Shang Simla Waterfall Crane Park.jpg|Crane Park |-| Videos= File:Meditation Sim Fu style|The music of Shang Simla File:Sims 3 World Adventures - China Trailer|The Sims 3 World Adventures - China Trailer ==Notes== ==Names in foreign languages== Excluding non-English languages where it's also called Shang Simla verbatim. {| class="wikitable sortable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" ! '''Al Simhara''' is a pre-made destination sub-world that was introduced in ''[[The Sims 3: World Adventures]]'' along with the other worlds [[Shang Simla]] and [[Champs Les Sims]].

==Overview==
[[File:W egypt.png|left]] Al Simhara is an ancient land built against a river, full of magic and mystery. It is a land of [[Mummy|mummies]], pyramids, and [[Fishing (The Sims 3)|crocodiles]]. It is found in [[wikipedia:Egypt|Egypt]] and features activities and items drawn from Egyptian culture. The name is a reference to the [[Wikipedia:Sahara Desert|Sahara Desert]] of Egypt. This town features fully explorable [[tomb]]s and [[hidden tomb]]s, including famous Egyptian landmarks such as the Pyramids, the Sphinx, and Temple of Queen Hatshepsut. Sims can explore these landmark tombs, thereby undertaking [[Al Simhara adventures|adventures]]. The company [[MorcuCorp]] features strongly in these adventures. It is an excellent subhood for [[Sim]]s to improve their [[Photography]] skill. There are numerous pre-made [[#Families|families]] in Al Simhara, although they all lack description texts and money. A trip to Al Simhara costs §1600 for one Sim and §1000 for each additional Sim.

===Features===
[[File:W egypt.png|thumb|200px]]
* At night a gentle glow lights up at the bases of the Pyramids.
* The entire world is so hot that there is a visible heat haze during the daylight hours.
* Another mine monster is found here, in addition to those in [[Sunset Valley]], [[Riverview]], and [[Twinbrook]].
* Mummies will be lurking the tombs in this destination, and they can curse Sims.
* There are more sims in this destination than in Champs Les Sims and Shang Simla.

===Exclusive Items===

* National dishes like Falafel and Shawarma, new recipes for the [[Cooking (The Sims 3)|cooking]] skill.
* The [[snake charming]] [[Secret skills|secret skill]] can be learned through a [[Snake Charming Basket|snake charming basket]] from the market.
* Expensive [[camera]]s for developing the [[Photography]] skill.
* [[Book]]s that are exclusive to Al Simhara, including a Photography skill book.
* New [[Fishing (The Sims 3)|fishing]] and [[Collecting (The Sims 3)|collecting]] items to gather, like crocodiles and copper.
* Also, like in [[Shang Simla]] and [[Champs Les Sims]] tomb survival items like the [[Shower-in-a-Can]] and [[dried food]] can be purchased.

== The Sims 3: World Adventures (smartphone) ==
[[File:Egyptpuzzle.png|thumb|The memory puzzle at Archeology Dig]]
''[[The Sims 3: World Adventures (smartphone)]]'' allows the player to send their sim abroad, either for §150 for an economy flight, or §250 for a first class flight. Egypt is one of the three locations.

In Egypt, a sim can complete two tours: Pyramids<ref>https://vimeo.com/881826493?share=copy#t=0</ref> and Sphinx<ref>https://vimeo.com/881826406?share=copy#t=0</ref>. Both tours are free, and consist of a presentation of various images of the site along with fun facts about it.
[[File:Archeologydig.jpg|thumb|A sim visiting the Archeology Dig]]
A sim can also visit the Archeology Dig, where they can complete a memory puzzle to find an ancient artifact. Artifacts can later be sold in the home neighborhood.

Next to the Archeology Dig is a Market, where a sim can shop for produce, buy street food, or practice bartering.

[[File:The_Llamafall.png|thumb|The Llamafall]]
*In ''[[The Sims 4: Get Together]]'', there's a fountain which is said to be an exact replica of a fountain unearthed in Al Simhara.
*In the texture files for ''[[The Sims 2: Bon Voyage]]'', there are two placeholder unused textures called '''wall-panel-hieroglyphics''' and '''wall-stone-pyramid''', suggesting that a desert destination may have originally been planned for that expansion.
*One of the empty lots, The Island Estate, is notable for being inaccessible by land, by water, and by tombs, the only pre-placed lot in a Maxis-built world to have this distinction after [[ocean swimming]] was introduced to The Sims 3. After [[The Sims 3/Patch 12|Patch 12]], it was possible to place a custom lot across the water gap to allow for a pedestrian [[bridge]] to the island, but placing it would cause all [[fish]] to disappear from the river. Changes made to [[Edit Town]] at later points (Most likely around [[The Sims 3/Patch 42|Patch 42]]) removed the ability to create such a bridge.

Here, the streets are lined with Sims in search of laughter, opportunity, and love—and maybe a few Simoleons, too. Moonlight Bay offers many places to shop, such as the funky bookstore, and the vibrant parks are almost always full of families enjoying nature to its fullest.}}{{Distinguish|Moonlight Falls}}
'''Moonlight Bay''' is the only [[neighborhood]] that shipped with the [[wikipedia:Xbox 360|Xbox 360]] and [[wikipedia:PlayStation 3|PlayStation 3]] versions of [[The Sims 3 (console)|The Sims 3]].<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YhQpipRogMU</ref> The [[wikipedia:Wii|Wii]] version uses a beach town known as [[Vista Beach]]<ref>[http://wii.gamespy.com/wii/the-sims-3/ The Sims 3 - Wii - GameSpy]</ref> and the [[Wikipedia:Nintendo DS|Nintendo DS]] version uses a separate neighborhood known as [[Beacon Bay]]. The neighborhood's name may be a pun on [[Sunset Valley]]. Although there are many families, only six are playable (excluding the families in the family bin), and only eight out of fifteen lots in the neighborhood can be lived in. It is possible to play as the other Sims by asking them to move in or by marrying them, but they can only live in the same house as the player.
== Overview ==
Moonlight Bay is a small coastal town surrounded on three sides by mountains. Like [[Sunset Valley]], Moonlight Bay mixes modern and futuristic building ideas with nostalgic architecture and design rooted in American suburbs of the 1950s. The town has its own school, bistro, bakery (actually a [[diner]]), library, art gallery, movie theatre and gymnasium. There are no empty lots when the game is first played. Most [[Rabbit hole|rabbit holes]] are located in the center of town, with another commercial district in the northwest. Residential lots come in three sizes: small, medium and large. Landmarks include the beach, the waterfall and the lighthouse.

The town's [[Rabbit hole|rabbit holes]], save for the [[Office building|business office]], [[police department]], [[abandoned warehouse]], and [[mausoleum]], are unique to the game, with all being "upgradeable" by reaching the final level of in the specific career each rabbit hole is tied to (or in the case of the [[school]], making the honor roll). Upon being promoted or making the honor roll, the rabbit hole's shell and name will both update to another exclusive design.

== Trivia ==
[[File:TS3Console MoonlightBay BETA E32010.png|thumb|The map view in the E3 2010 build of the game. Several differences are noted.]]
* The town, as showcased at E3 2010, has some peculiar differences from the final product:<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CsWgkXTF-bw</ref>
** Park community lots originally had more specific icons instead of the generic pond icon. Some names are different (beta -> final):
*** Street names are abbreviated (e.g.  Haskins '''Wy.''' -> Haskins '''Way''')
*** Moonlight '''Cove''' Public Beach -> Moonlight '''Bay''' Public Beach
*** Supermarket -> EverFresh Delights Grocery
** The grass, trees, cliffs, and mountains were more simple and saturated.
** The [[spa]] and [[Office building|business office]] lots were originally going to use the base game's Sunset Valley rabbit holes (Sharma Day Spa and Doo Peas Corporate Tower respectively), rather than the Happy Go Luxury Day Spa and the Riverview/Twinbrook office shell in the final game.
*** Strangely, in the final game, the map icons for both still resemble the beta rabbit holes, rather than the ones used.
** There is a modern cubic lot called "Casa Del Fiesta" in place of the Landgraabs' Mediterranean Villa house.
** There was originally a second [[Pool (lot)|pool]] lot where the [[Fishing spot|Industrious Industries Research Pond]] is now. Interestingly, the pool can still be seen in one of the game's loading screens for said area, as shown in the gallery above.
*Fans recreation of this world can be found in [[Talk:Moonlight_Bay|talk page]].

Sugar Maple Coast.text:
{{Era|TS3PETSC}}
{{Infobox world

'''Sugar Maple Coast''' is a pre-made [[neighborhood]] included with [[The Sims 3: Pets (console)|''The Sims 3: Pets'' for console]]. It was first showcased at GamesCom 2011. The world includes the standard [[community lot]]s, as well as several new lots exclusive to the game.<ref>[http://www.thesimshub.com/2011/09/the-sims-hubs-pets-qa-and-exclusive-screenshot/ The Sims Hub - The Sims 3: Pets Q&A and Exclusive Screenshot]</ref>{{Deadlink}}

The world’s design and atmosphere are similar to [[Appaloosa Plains]] and [[Port Abel]], featuring rustic scenery, rolling hills, and a smaller community. Sugar Maple Coast also includes a variety of new [[rabbit holes]], such as a [[pet center]] and a [[Lighthouse#The Sims 3: Pets (console)|lighthouse]], and utilizes combined map tags previously seen in neighborhoods such as [[Bridgeport]].

== Overview ==
Sugar Maple Coast is a coastal town reminiscent of New England-style architecture. It is considerably smaller than other worlds due to the use of combined rabbit holes. According to various in-game text and biographies, the town was founded by the crews of ''Queen Bella’s Revenge'' and ''The Hawthorne'', including [[Samuel Gilman]], [[Max Dalton]], [[List of minor Sims|Mario Angel]], and [[Timaeus Goth]], who docked at its coastal ridges long ago. Originally named '''Gilman Hill''' in honor of its first captain, the settlement was later renamed Sugar Maple Coast to enshrine the various sugar maple trees surrounding the coast as the population expanded. At some point, the [[Goth family|Goth]] clan left the town, implied to have settled elsewhere. Currently, many of the families residing in Sugar Maple Coast are descended from the town’s original founders, with additional families establishing residence, preserving the town’s historical heritage.

Like [[Appaloosa Plains]] and [[Port Abel]], pets are an essential component of the world. They can easily traverse the neighborhood, as many community lots feature [[Food bowl|food bowls]] for Sims to fill. Pets can pursue one of five different [[Career (pet)|careers]], four of which depend on the species of the employed animal. When traveling, pets are transported in a special blue [[Taxicab|taxi]] adorned with pet-themed stickers. Sims can also enroll their pets in skill classes or pamper them at the new [[pet center]].

Sugar Maple Coast introduces several new exploratory [[Rabbit hole|rabbit holes]], including the [[Abandoned mine#The Sims 3: Pets (console)|abandoned mine]], the [[Lighthouse#The Sims 3: Pets (console)|lighthouse]], and the [[Cave#The Sims 3: Pets (console)|coastal cave]]. Each of these locations ties into the town’s history and provides new interactive pop-ups when explored. Pets exploring these areas will encounter unique flavor text specific to each rabbit hole.

The world borrows several elements from [[The Sims 3: Ambitions|''The Sims 3: Ambitions'']], such as the [[Inventing|inventing skill]] & [[Scraptronic™ Workbench|workbench]], [[junkyard]], and creation of [[SimBot|SimBots]]. Additionally, components of the [[Ghost hunter|ghost hunting]] and [[investigator]] professions were reworked into random midnight hauntings and the [[Mystery Journal|mystery journal]] feature, respectively.

== Lots ==
There are two starter lots available for new households. Additionally, the player can choose from four pre-made families at the start of the game. Two haunted houses, the Old Gilman Farmstead and [[313 Harvest Nook|Goth Manor]], can be unlocked during gameplay, bringing the total number of editable residential lots to eight. Non-playable family homes cannot be occupied or edited by the player.

The six standard residential lots each have a selection of bin houses available that the player can use to replace their current home, similar to the [[Family bin|Library]] from the PC version; most lots have three replacement options, while the two largest lots offer two. The two haunted houses do not have any replacement lots available. If the active family dies, the haunted houses will remain unlocked on the same save file, allowing the player to generate a new family and continue living in them.

:''Brady and Brooke seem to have the perfect marriage and family. He is a popular and respected journalist and she is the hometown sports star. Their son Brock seems to be following in his mother's footsteps and is an accomplished angler. Yes, life is good! But can this ideal family survive Molly, Brooke's crazy aunt, moving in? Brooke invited her to visit and now she seems like she's here to stay. Brady puts on a good face but Molly's antics are certainly wearing him down.''

Those few who do know her describe her as excitable, inappropriate and overall odd. Her father Zachariah is truly an enigma. Vincent and his wife find themselves overworked at times between the pressures of careers and a new child.''

:§48,500

This has been great for his career, but not so much when it comes to his family. His wife has grown used to his ways over the years. However, the kids chafe from his need for everything to be perfect. Andrew particularly worries for his teenage son Andy, who seems to want to do nothing but play Planet of SimCraft.''

Whiskerton.title: Whiskerton
Whiskerton.text:
{{Era|NH}} {{Infobox neighborhood |name = Whiskerton |image = [[File:Whiskerton (console).png|250px]] |caption = |game = The Sims 2 Pets (console) |housed residents = 12
4 (PSP) |townies = 13
8 (PSP) }} '''Whiskerton''' is the neighborhood where ''[[The Sims 2: Pets (console)|The Sims 2: Pets]]'' for PlayStation 2, PSP, GameCube and Wii takes place. Whiskerton is the default neighborhood name and can be changed to another name. ==PS2, Wii and GameCube version== In ''The Sims 2: Pets'', the center of the neighborhood is a lake surrounded by land. It also features a waterfall with one lot called [[Lemming Point]] which is unoccupied, but a little south is a lot occupied by the [[Hardiman family|Hardiman]] family in [[Serenity Falls]]. On the far side to the right is a country like setting with two lots occupied by the [[Simpson family|Simpson]] family at [[Feline Farms]] and the [[Newbie family|Newbie]] family at [[Cozy Acres]]. South of the neighborhood is an island with one unoccupied lot called [[Fishbone Island]]. Most of the neighborhood is surrounded by pine trees. ===Families=== *'''[[Newbie family|Newbie]]''': [[Bob Newbie]], [[Betty Newbie]], [[Buddy Newbie]] Lives In: [[Cozy Acres]] Funds: §3,562 When beginning the tutorial the player will start with [[Bob Newbie|Bob]] and eventually switch to [[Betty Newbie|Betty]]. Both Betty and Bob have 3 points in cooking, they live in a tidy cozy home near the country fields. *'''[[Simpson family|Simpson]]''': [[Dottie Simpson]], [[Oscar Simpson]], [[Smokey Simpson]], [[Bella Simpson]], [[Daisy Simpson]], [[Shnookems Simpson]] Lives In: [[Feline Farms]] Funds: §1,111 Dottie owns 5 cats and lives in a house dominated with feline features. A rooster crow is heard often at this lot. *'''[[Oakely family|Oakely]]''': [[Buck Oakely]], [[Hamhock Oakely]], [[Lucky Oakely]], [[Rufus Oakely]] Lives In: [[Dogwood Forest]] Funds: §4,315 Buck has 3 dogs and lives in a cabin like home surrounded by pine trees and "Gnarly Carly Hardwood" trees. His home, like most homes in Whiskerton, is located in front of the lake. *'''[[Hardiman family|Hardiman]]''': [[Dan Hardiman]], [[Kate Hardiman]], [[Buster Hardiman]] Lives In: [[Serenity Falls]] Funds: §4,498 The Hardimans live in a lavish classical theme home with the waterfall located behind their home. North West from the home there is a [[bridge]]. West of the home is a beige coloured home with a red tile roof. Also East from the home is a tunnel that leads probably to [[Lemming Point]], though it is uncertain. *'''[[Townsend family|Townsend]]''': [[Linda Townsend]], [[William Townsend]], [[Henrietta Townsend]], [[Fauntleroy Townsend]] Lives In: [[Paw Valley Road]] Funds: §8,986 The Townsends lives with 2 dogs. Their home is modern and features a beautiful view at the back of the lake and the waterfall, in the far side most of the sim's homes can be seen here (not interacted with though). In front a mountain range can be seen. *'''[[May household|May]]''': [[Mira May]], [[Penelope Arnold]], [[Varian Parker]], [[Marsha Worthington]], [[Presto Parker]], [[Falafel May]] Lives In: [[Firefly Lake]] Funds: §2,328 The May household consists of 4 different Sims, meaning they're not all "May's", as it's Mira's home and the others are her tenants. The lot features a tiny beach behind the lot with an outstanding view of the lake. The home is surrounded by shrubs. Much north to the view of the lake is the country side and a canyon of sorts. ===Unoccupied lots=== In order of price: *[[Rock Ridge]] - §8,500 *[[Redwood Glen]] - §8,500 *[[Fishbone Island]] - §14,000 *[[Lemming Point]] - §14,000 ===Townies=== As the player progresses through the game by raising relationships and fulfilling wants, other Sims are unlocked. Players cannot start a game with these Sims but they can move them into already inhabited households by marrying them or simply increasing their relationship points with them enough to ask them to move in. Until a Sim is unlocked they will not appear around the Town Square or visit/be seen walking by their home. The last known Townies to unlock are Eddie and Joyce Howard and their 2 dogs and 1 cat. Here are a list of the townies unlocked and the aspiration points totals: *[[Charlie Prescott]] - 100 *[[Patty Prescott]] - 100 *[[Cindy Lou Boyle]] - 100 *[[Claire Seville]] - 1000 *[[Hilary Duff]] - 1000 *[[Walter Mellon]] - 1000 *[[Wanda Mellon]] - 1000 *[[Babette Lambert]] - 10000 *[[Jim Lester]] - 10000 *[[Huckleberry Wong]] - 10000 *[[Kiki Pickens]] - 25000 *[[Timothy Pickens]] - 25000 *[[Eddie Howard]] - 35000 *[[Joyce Howard]] - 35000 ===Town Square=== The Town Square in Whiskerton is basically a [[park]]. The currency here is [[Pet Points]] and the town square introduces pet stores and drink/ice cream stalls. The more pet points are spent the more the town square expands as well the shop that was shopped in. For example, if the spends enough pet points in the [[Pet Emporium]], it will grow bigger and more objects will be available. The Town Square has a [[chess table]], drinking fountains, vending machines, a park fountain (which will expand), bathroom stalls and a statue (also will expand). It is unknown where it is located in Whiskerton as it doesn't show it in the neighborhood view, but it is known to be near the lake as it sits on the edge of it and can be seen in the background. ==PSP version== [[File:Whiskerton.jpg|thumb|250px|PSP version of Whiskerton]] The PSP version is smaller and only features four lots or sections and very few families. The town square is also a bit degraded. The four sections consists of ''Ruff Woods'' and cabin like section. ''Birmatown'' a city-like theme similar to [[Bridgeport]]. ''Pupville'' is a peaceful neighborhood. Lastly, ''Kitty Heights,'' a very upscale section with a home that has two [[simoleon]] signs on top. ===Families=== *'''Townsend''': [[Linda Townsend]], [[William Townsend]], [[Falafel May]], [[Presto Parker]] Lives In: [[Ruff Woods]] Funds: §12,543 Like all homes with preset families in the [[The Sims 2 Pets (console)|PSP]] version, the home is small and uses Bedroom set 1, studio, Layout 1. The scenery behind the home is similar to the home in ''Dogwood Forest''. Also [[Falafel May|Falafel]] & [[Presto Parker|Presto]] which were in the May family are now in the Townsends. [[Presto Parker|Presto]] has a brown fur colour rather than the black one in the other console versions and [[Linda Townsend|Linda]] wears a different outfit. *'''Newbie''': [[Bob Newbie]] , [[Betty Newbie]], [[Buddy Newbie]] Lives In: [[Pupville]] Funds: §16,632 The lot is surrounded by neighborhood homes with white walls and black or red tiled roofs and is fenced. ===Family bin/real estate office families=== Most families which appear in the PS2, GameCube and Wii versions are in the family bin. These are: *'''May''': [[Mira May]], [[Penelope Arnold]], [[Varian Parker]], [[Marsha Worthington]] *'''Oakley''': [[Buck Oakely]], [[Hamhock Oakely]], [[Lucky Oakely]], [[Rufus Oakely]] *'''Simpson''': [[Dottie Simpson]], [[Bella Simpson]], [[Daisy Simpson]], [[Shnookems Simpson]] *'''Hardiman''': [[Dan Hardiman]], [[Kate Hardiman]], [[Buster Hardiman]] ==Trivia== *The name of the neighborhood is a reference to [[Wikipedia:Whiskers|whiskers]], which are long, thick hair around the mouth of some animals, mostly mammals such as [[cat]]s and [[Small pet|mice]]. *If the player leaves the [[neighborhood]] screen for a while, the screen will change from morning, to noon, to evening. *A portion of the lake can be seen in the PSP version on the neighborhood screen. *The [[chess table]] is replaced with a [[dining table]] and the tiles in the bathroom are replaced with red [[carpet]] in the Town Square in the PSP version. *Whiskerton is referenced in [[The Sims 3: Pets (console)|''The Sims 3: Pets'']] for console, as a [[Relic#The Sims 3: Pets (console)|relic]] called "The Whiskerton [[Plumbob|Plumbob"]] can be dug up. {{clrr}} {{TSCNeighborhoods}} [[pt-br:Whiskerton]] [[nl:Snorhaarlem]] [[es:Villa Bigotes]] [[pl:Simowo]] [[Category:The Sims 2: Pets (console)]]

:§64,520

:''Henry and his dog Simon have been training for the upcoming SimCity Dog Show for months now. He is confident he will win, but he faces stiff competition from Diana DeBore.''

*'''[[Carter family]]''' ''1344 Buddy Street''
:§545
:[[Melissa Carter]], [[Bruno Carter]]

:§358,100

:''Diana DeBore is a rich and ruthless landowner who wants to own all of Garden Heights. She was once a talented dog trainer, and her dog Precious is a recently retired SimCity Dog Show champion, but events are pushing Diana to re-enter the dog show for one last time.''

*'''[[Flores family]]''' ''1361 Dargail Lane''
:§5,632
:[[Amaya Flores]], [[Roscoe Flores]]
:''Amaya has lived in Garden Heights for as long as Alice Whitt. She and Alice are the best of friends. Amaya's dog Roscoe is friendly and playful, but very hyper. Amaya is always looking for romantic fun with no lasting attachments.''

*'''[[Grinder family]]''' ''1364 Dargail Lane''
:§9,109
:[[Coach Grinder]], [[Meat Grinder]]
:''Coach Grinder and his dog Meat might seem content to be left alone, but Coach is actually loads of fun at parties and Meat is surprisingly friendly with people who get to know him.''

*'''[[Jones family (Garden Heights)|Jones family]]''' ''1330 Vista del Arroyo''
:§2,299
:[[Thomas Jones]], [[Lucy Jones]]
:''Thomas has secretly been in love with Alice for years, but he is too shy to let her know his true feelings. When Alice unexpectedly moves back to Garden Heights, Thomas wonders if he has been given another chance to let her know how he really feels. Thomas yearns to be a police officer but feels he is not qualified. Perhaps his timidity and shyness will crumble when he finds his courage by helping Alice as much as he can.''

*'''[[Mustella family]]''' ''1314 Pal Avenue''
:§2,795
:[[Reece Mustella]], [[Brock Thornton]], [[Indie Thornton]]
:''Brock and Reece are common street thugs who work for Diana DeBore as henchmen for hire. Brock is the muscle, while Reece is the brain. Brock is a victim of circumstance who took the only job he could find, working with Reece. Brock may look tough but is secretly quite the softie, especially when it comes to pets.''

*'''[[Whitt family]]''' ''1362 Dargail Lane''
:§121,833
:[[Alice Whitt]], [[Sam Whitt]]
:''Alice Whitt has inherited her grandparents' house. Recently she's moved back to Garden Heights to take ownership of the property, but money problems have put her on the verge of financial ruin. A starving artist, she hasn't been able to make ends meet every month, but she is determined to make a better life for herself and her dog Sam.''

'''Felicity Island''' is one of the [[neighborhood]]s shipped with ''[[The Sims Castaway Stories]]'', where the [[Shipwrecked and Single]] story takes place. The neighborhood enters free play mode once the player completes the main storyline.

==Lots==
The lots on Felicity Island all have travel portals instead of the normal roads seen in all other neighborhoods. Each lot has at least one, although many of the [[community lot]]s have several that lead to specific areas on the travel map (the image in the gallery below). During the [[Shipwrecked and Single]] story, some of the community lots temporarily become [[residential lot]]s.

*'''[[Heimata family]]''' ''The Heimata Family''
:Resources: 2,530

:[[Ahio Heimata]], [[Rainui Heimata]]
:''The Heimata family are among the most notable people on Felicity Island. Rainui is famous for her drama queen ways, and Ahio is famous for being able to put up with her.''

*'''[[Herenui family]]''' ''The Women's Hut''
:Resources: 3,015
:Food: 200
:[[Kiri Roimata]], [[Orama Herenui]], [[Tumata Tehea]]
:''By custom, the unattached women of the tribe live in huts in this jungle clearing. This fosters a sense of sharing and community, and makes lighter work out of daily living for all.''

*'''[[Manave family]]''' ''The Chief's Hut''
:Resources: 2,515
:Food: 250
:[[Fangaloka Manave]], [[Huhana Manave]], [[Nanihi Manave]]
:''The Manave family are close-knit, loving, and easygoing, despite bearing the weight of leading the tribe. Luckily, Fangaloka has developed a good relationship with all known predators over the years.''

:Resources: 3,000

:[[Amanaki Tama]], [[Urari Tama]], [[Afi Mohea]], [[Patariki Hina]], [[Winford Rhinehart]] (optional)
:''The Tamas were Felicity Island's shamans, herbalists, and all-round mystics. Amanaki Tama appointed a heroic outsider to succeed him as shaman, since no one in his own family was suited to take over the role.

*'''[[Whetu family]]''' ''The Men's Hut''
:Resources: 3,015
:Food: 
:[[Akolo Mamanu]], [[Emobi Whetu]], [[Timoti Fekitoa]]
:''By custom, the unattached men of the tribe live together in this hut. The friendship they share as a group alleviates their individual loneliness... for now.

===[[Family bin]] families===
*'''[[Rarahu Anuata|Anuata family]]'''
:Resources: 6,000
:[[Rarahu Anuata]]
:''Felicity Island's resident nomad Rarahu doesn't have a home, because he didn't want his prey to get familiar with his scent. But he's getting tired of carrying his collection of blankets everywhere, so he has been reconsidering his lifestyle.''

*'''[[Hugh Bailey|Bailey family]]'''
:Resources: 5,000
:[[Hugh Bailey]]
:''After Hugh nearly crashed the escape helicopter in a struggle over the radio, the pilot dropped him back off on Felicity Island. “You’ll be hearing from my lawyer!” Hugh shouted after the pilot, and he still plans to make good on that threat -- right after he finds a telephone, and calls his broker.''

*'''[[Sandra Barnham|Barnham family]]'''
:Resources: 5,250
:[[Sandra Barnham]]
:''Sandra means well, she’s just a little out of touch with the lives of workaday Sims. Unfortunately, she mentioned her prize begonias once too often for the escape helicopter pilot's liking. Now she'll have plenty of time to cultivate the native flora of Felicity Island.''

*'''[[David Bennett|Bennett family]]'''
:Resources: 7,500
:[[David Bennett]]
:''Your mechanical skills were good enough to earn you a working passage on the Solomon Queen to the hottest singles resort in the world, Club Meet Your Mate. Now that you're shipwrecked, your survival skills are going to require as much work as the ship's engines did.''

*'''[[Gina Gibson|Gibson family]]'''
:Resources: 5,500
:[[Gina Gibson]]
:''Rescue had arrived, but Gina and the other castaways had a little difficulty staying on the pilot's good side. Before being dumped back on Felicity Island, Gina learned an important lesson -- when asking a helicopter pilot for "lessons," always wait for his answer before grabbing the control stick.''

*'''[[Jessica Knight|Knight family]]'''
:Resources: 7,500
:[[Jessica Knight]]
:''Writing an article on Club Meet Your Mate for "Going Places" magazine was a great opportunity, until that unfortunate shipwreck incident. If you can improve your survival skills enough, and hang in until rescue, you might be able to sell this story as a movie of the week.''

*'''[[Smith family (Felicity Island)|Smith family]]'''
:Resources: 6,000
:[[Robby Smith]], [[Emma Langsford]]
:''Much to their surprise, Robby and Emma found happiness on Felicity Island. Now that they've decided to stay, will they grow closer to one another or will they simply drive each other nuts?''

Wanmami Island.title: Wanmami Island
Wanmami Island.text:
{{era|NH|CS}} {{Infobox neighborhood |name = Wanmami Island |image = [[File:Wanmami Neighborhood.png|250px]] |game = The Sims Castaway Stories |caption = Wanmami Island is home to the local, the lost, and the long-range mariner. Rising majestically out of the vast blue ocean, the island looks inviting enough. There are numerous suitable places to make camp, and nothing particularly dangerous or ominous is visible from the water. The natives named it "Wanmami," after the fevered whimpering often heard from shipwreck survivors washed ashore on the beach. |housed residents = 11 |family bin sims = 5 |townies = 30}}
From the air, Wanmami doesn't look especially unlike any other somewhat-inhabited island, but for the handful of plane crash and shipwreck survivors whose ways have been found here by malfunction-induced circumstance, it's a welcome return to dry land. The sun always shines on Wanmami Island except when it sets, and the weather is exactly as ordered in a tropical paradise.
'''Wanmami Island''' is a Free Play mode [[neighborhood]] shipped with ''[[The Sims Castaway Stories]]''. Playable [[Sim]]s in this neighborhood can purchase story rewards from the Story Rewards Bin, once they have been unlocked during the [[Shipwrecked and Single]] story at [[Felicity Island]]. New lots cannot be created without the use of third-party mods and programs (such as [[Package editor#SimPE|SimPE]]). Willville.text:
{{Era|NH|TSC}}

|family bin sims  = 5
